name: Insurance broker pipeline
summary: See every renewal coming and keep new business moving. Lead to bound with the advice documented before the offer, plus a renewal case for each policy that opens 120 to 45 days before expiry.
description: Renewals slip past and advice goes undocumented when new business and renewals live in separate lists or in your head. This template runs both side by side: opportunities from the first inquiry through needs analysis, quotes, offer and decision to a bound policy, an advice-documented date on every offer, and policies with their renewal date that open a renewal case on their own. It holds a reference to the advice record and to the policy in your agency system, never health data, claims details, bank details or identity copies. It is not policy administration, a comparison or rating engine, claims handling or commission reconciliation.

page.metaDescription: Never miss a renewal. Paste this template into Claude, ChatGPT or Codex: your agent builds an insurance broker CRM with advice records and renewal cases.
page.headline: Never miss a renewal: an insurance broker CRM your AI agent builds for new business and renewals
page.answer: An insurance broker CRM runs two pipelines side by side: new business from inquiry to bound policy, and a renewal case for every policy that opens well before it expires. Paste this template into your AI agent and it builds both in Customermates, with the advice documented before every offer. You approve the plan before anything is built. Policy data stays in your agency system.

routine.title: The broker's weekly desk routine
steps: Open the renewals coming up: commercial policies from about 120 days before expiry, personal lines from about 45 days. Give each case an owner and a first step.
Chase the insurers for quotes that are late, and the clients who have not answered a renewal offer after a week.
Check that every offer carries the date of the advice record, so the needs analysis is documented before the offer goes out. Follow each offer up the day after you present it.
Confirm the client's decision about 30 days before renewal, ahead of the notice date of the contract.
Call new clients a week after the policy is bound, and write to the client when your agency system reports an unpaid premium.

limits: It is not your agency management system or policy administration. Policies, premiums and commission statements stay in your agency system; here you keep a reference and the renewal date.
It is not a comparison or rating engine. Quotes come from carrier portals and comparison tools, and you record the result.
It does not handle claims, underwriting submissions or commission reconciliation.
It stores no health data, claims details, bank details or identity copies, and not the advice record itself: only its date and a link to where you keep it.
It does not produce or certify advice. It records that the advice was documented before the offer; the advice is yours, and the duties that apply depend on your country.
It has no mass mailing, sequences, telephony or SMS. Messages are individual drafts that you review and send.

faq.question: What is the difference between an agency system and a CRM for a broker?
faq.answer: The agency management system holds policies, premiums, documents and commission statements. A CRM holds the relationship and the next step: who asked, which quote is open, which renewal is coming and who calls whom by when. This template is the second layer and keeps only references to the first.

faq.question: How long before expiry should I start a renewal?
faq.answer: It differs by line and country. Sources suggest about 90 to 120 days for commercial policies and 30 to 45 days for personal lines. The template opens a commercial renewal case 120 days before expiry and a personal one 45 days before, and you can change both. Notice periods differ by country and contract, so check the policy for the real deadline.

faq.question: Do I have to document advice before an offer?
faq.answer: In the EU the Insurance Distribution Directive requires a needs analysis before a contract is concluded, and many countries expect the advice to be documented. The details depend on your country and on whether you act as broker or agent, so check your own duties. The template records the date of the advice and a link to where it is stored, and shows offers that have none. This is not legal advice.

faq.question: Can I store policy and health data in the CRM?
faq.answer: Store as little as possible: a reference or link to the policy, the line, the renewal date and the annual premium. Health data, claims details, bank details and identity copies stay out, and Customermates has no field-level permissions to hide single columns. Keep the documents in your agency system or in a document store with access control.

faq.question: Does the agent write to my clients?
faq.answer: No. The prompt tells the agent to send nothing and to create no sample records. Drafts exist only when you ask for them, and you send them yourself.

prompt.intro: I run a broker book and renewals sneak up on me, while I also have to document the advice before every offer. Set up an insurance broker pipeline in my Customermates workspace: new business from lead to bound with the advice documented before the offer, policies with a renewal date and a renewal case for each, and dated follow-ups. Store no health data, claims details or identity copies.
